rfi.title: Tanzania's Hassan makes historic Russia visit amid frayed ties with West
rfi.description: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan begins a three-day state visit to Russia on Wednesday – the first official trip by a Tanzanian head of state to Moscow since 1969 – as her government faces growing criticism from Western countries over violence linked to the country's 2025 elections.

rfi.title: EU unveils plan to cut dependence on US and Asian technology
rfi.description: Europe is launching a sweeping push to reduce its dependence on American and Asian technology, with plans to boost homegrown chips, cloud computing and artificial intelligence while keeping greater control over data and key digital services.

rfi.title: El Nino threat grows as Europe prepares for another hot summer
rfi.description: The warming El Nino climate phenomenon is likely to develop by the end of August, the United Nations' weather agency said, raising the risk of extreme weather as Europe faces another summer on the front line of climate change.

rfi.title: Faye appoints cabinet despite Sonko's Pastef boycott threat
rfi.description: Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has appointed a new government, despite an initial threat by his own party to boycott the process. Pastef, led by former prime minister Ousmane Sonko, said it would not participate, citing disagreements over the cabinet's composition, but five of its members ultimately appeared on the final list.

rfi.title: EU tightens migration rules, eyes strategic enlargement in Balkans
rfi.description: The European Union has reached a deal on tougher migration rules that would allow countries to set up so-called “return hubs” outside the bloc, a move hailed by supporters as a practical answer to stalled deportations, but denounced by rights groups as a dangerous step towards offshore detention. Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

rfi.title: Macron to meet Hungary's PM Magyar to discuss Ukraine, European defence
rfi.description: Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar meets French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace on Wednesday, as the two leaders look to strengthen European support for Ukraine following the end of Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule.

rfi.title: Players to watch: England's Harry Kane is chasing history
rfi.description: Harry Kane will play for England at a third World Cup this summer, at the age of 32. In the second instalment of a five-part series on players to watch at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at the World Cup career of England's record goalscorer.

rfi.title: WHO seeks more aid for Congo as ebola outbreak continues to spread
rfi.description: The head of the World Health Organization  met with Félix Tshisekedi on Monday to discuss the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, as an aid agency warned the epidemic was likely far larger than official figures suggest. The government said confirmed Ebola cases had risen to 321.

rfi.title: French health minister promises fast track access to mental health for youth
rfi.description: France's Health Minister Stéphanie Rist announced on Tuesday that the government would fast-track access to mental health appointments for young people. She promised that those identified by staff in the national education system as having mental health problems would be seen by a professional within 24 to 48 hours.

rfi.title: New York Times chief slams AI companies for 'theft' of intellectual property
rfi.description: The head of The New York Times newspaper launched a scathing attack on artificial intelligence companies, accusing them of "shameless theft of intellectual property" and of threatening journalism. He was speaking at a global media congress on Monday in the southern French city of Marseille.

rfi.title: Cattelan’s famous taped banana stolen from French museum

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Morocco, African champions by ruling

Associations et syndicats multiplient les prises de position pour marquer leur hostilité à ce choix.

lemonde.description: Selon la procureure d’Auch, le suspect mis en examen pour l’enlèvement de Lyhanna avait fait l’objet de signalements et de plaintes pour des faits impliquant des mineurs depuis 2017.

lemonde.title: Les New York Knicks en finale NBA : l’abandon gagnant de la politique des stars, comme au PSG
lemonde.description: L’équipe new-yorkaise dispute, mercredi, le premier match des finales de la ligue nord-américaine de basket-ball contre les Spurs de Victor Wembanyama. A l’instar du Paris Saint-Germain, les Knicks ont dû se réinventer après des années difficiles.

lemonde.title: Jacques Toubon : « Le temps est venu de faire une alliance politique pour reconstruire l’exception culturelle »
lemonde.description: Après l’affaire Grasset et la tribune anti-Bolloré à Cannes, l’ancien ministre de la culture plaide, dans un entretien au « Monde », en faveur d’une nouvelle politique culturelle pour 2027 et s’inquiète de la dérive de sa famille politique vers l’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : Benyamin Nétanyahou affirme « être d’accord » avec Donald Trump « sur les points principaux concernant l’Iran »

lemonde.title: Affaire Xavier Dupont de Ligonnès : M6 piégée par un faux prêtre, l’émission « Appel à témoins » contrainte de s’excuser

lemonde.title: « Le cliché, c’est Sarkozy ou les chaussures bateau » : la colocation de Quentin, 25 ans, à Neuilly-sur-Seine
lemonde.description: « Et toi, t’habites où ? ». En pleine crise du logement, étudiants et jeunes actifs redéfinissent, souvent malgré eux, l’art de trouver un chez-soi. Cette semaine, Quentin en témoigne : après des expériences dans des chambres sans âme ou insalubres de la capitale, le Nazairien a réalisé son rêve d’adolescent en partageant un trois-pièces avec son meilleur ami.

lemonde.title: Chlordécone aux Antilles : la loi adoptée au Parlement largement édulcorée
lemonde.description: La responsabilité de l’Etat a été ramenée à sa « part de responsabilité » par le Sénat, et l’introduction souhaitée de la notion de « préjudice d’anxiété » a été refusée par le gouvernement. La dépollution des terres reste un « objectif », et le texte ne prévoit rien de nouveau concernant l’indemnisation des victimes.

lemonde.title: Le physicien Thierry Dauxois reçoit un avis favorable du Parlement pour prendre la tête du CNRS
lemonde.description: A la tête de l’Institut de physique du CNRS depuis 2021, ce fin connaisseur du plus grand organisme de recherche français devrait bientôt en être nommé PDG. Devant les élus du peuple, Thierry Dauxois a déclaré vouloir défendre la liberté académique et maintenir les recrutements malgré la crise budgétaire que traverse l’institution.

lemonde.title: Carlos Ghosn, un fugitif très actif

lemonde.description: Quatre-vingts ans après le référendum constitutionnel de 1946 qui a instauré la République et ouvert le vote aux femmes, le texte fondamental né de l’antifascisme demeure un repère politique et identitaire consensuel.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros : Kostyuk contre Andreeva, une demi-finale sur fond de guerre en Ukraine
france24fr.description: Après son quart de finale face à sa compatriote Elina Svitolina, Marta Kostyuk est devenue la première Ukrainienne à se qualifier pour une demi-finale de Roland-Garros. Une visite inédite validée par les descendants de Gustave Eiffel permet de revivre sa construction.

france24fr.title: L'aéroport de Koweït City en feu après un attaque iranienne, au moins un mort et 63 blessés
france24fr.description: L'aéroport international du Koweït a été touché par des drones iraniens, faisant au moins un mort et plusieurs blessés. L’attaque a provoqué une suspension du trafic et encore davantage fragilisé le cessez-le-feu en place entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Récit de Nina Masson et Solange Mougin.

france24fr.title: Deux secouristes tués dans une frappes israélienne sur le sud du Liban
france24fr.description: Une frappe israélienne a touché mercredi les environs de Beyrouth. L’armée poursuit également ses raids dans le sud du Liban, où au moins six personnes ont été tuées, dont deux secouristes. Récit de Nina Masson et Maxence Oudotte.

france24fr.title: Le prodige Français Victor Wembanyama à quatre victoires d'un premier titre NBA
france24fr.description: Victor Wembanyama jouera dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi sa première finale NBA avec les San Antonio Spurs, à seulement 22 ans, face aux Knicks de New York. Après sept matchs d’anthologie, le prodige français a reçu ce dimanche le titre de meilleur joueur des finales de la Conférence Ouest. Un récit de Jules Boiteau.

france24fr.title: Masculinistes, suprémacistes, complotistes : le "Davos" russe en croisade contre l'Occident "dépravé"
france24fr.description: Plusieurs célébrités et figures d’extrême droite se sont rendues en Russie à l'occasion du Forum économique de Saint-Pétersbourg, surnommé depuis les années 1990 le "Davos" russe, qui ouvre ses portes mercredi. Un étrange mélange de personnalités aussi controversées que le masculiniste Andrew Tate est censé donner une bonne image de la Russie de Vladimir Poutine.

france24fr.title: Wim Wenders retire "Faux Mouvement", film de 1975 montrant Nastassja Kinski nue adolescente
france24fr.description: Le réalisateur allemand Wim Wenders a annoncé mercredi retirer son film "Faux Mouvement", sorti en 1975, en raison d'une scène où l'actrice Nastassja Kinski, alors âgée de 13 ans, est montrée seins nus. L'actrice allemande luttait depuis dix ans pour faire supprimer la scène du long-métrage.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle en Colombie : icône de la gauche ou milliardaire soutenu par Trump ?
france24fr.description: Le second tour de la présidentielle en Colombie verra s'affronter un allié du président de gauche sortant Gustavo Petro et un avocat millionnaire, Abelardo de la Espriella, admirateur de Donald Trump et prônant la fermeté contre le crime. Donald Trump lui a apporté sons outien "total et complet", assurant sur son réseau Truth Social voir en lui un "dirigeant intelligent, fort et dur" qui va "stopper l'immigration illégale" et "restaurer l'ordre". Précisions de Léa Hurel, correspondante de France

france24fr.title: Assaut du Capitole : Trump renonce finalement à créer un fonds d'indemnisation pour les condamnés
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a finalement renoncé à son projet "anti-instrumentalisation" de la justice, tout juste créé. Cette annonce survient après la décision d’un tribunal d’en geler le fonds. Les démocrates ont dénoncé une "caisse noire" destinée à rétribuer les partisans de Donald Trump, y compris des personnes condamnées pour l'assaut du Capitole, sanctuaire de la démocratie américaine, le 6 janvier 2021. Précisions de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant de France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: Au Japon, un ours attaque un ouvrier devant son usine, casse une porte vitrée, puis disparaît
france24fr.description: Que feriez-vous si vous faisiez face à un ours ? La question vous paraît peut-être saugrenue, mais elle se pose de plus en plus fréquemment dans le quotidien des japonais. Le pays a enregistré mardi une nouvelle attaque, dans deux usines d'un quartier résidentiel. L'année dernière, treize personnes sont mortes suite à une confrontation avec un ours au Japon… un record. Récit d’Alexandra Quarini.

france24fr.title: Russie : des drones ukrainiens endommagent des sites militaires à Saint-Pétersbourg
france24fr.description: Des drones ukrainiens ont frappé mercredi un ⁠terminal pétrolier à ​Saint-Pétersbourg et un navire de guerre dans une base navale voisine, quelques heures avant l'ouverture du grand forum économique russe organisé par Vladimir Poutine. Cette attaque survient alors que les frappes s'intensifient de part et d'autre depuis plusieurs jours. Précisions de Gulliver Cragg, correspondant de France 24 à Kiev, et analyse de Patrick Martin-Genier, spécialiste des questions européennes et internationales.

france24fr.title: Israël bombarde le Sud du Liban et Beyrouth, au moins 6 morts près de Tyr
france24fr.description: L'Iran conditionne toujours tout accord avec les États-Unis à un respect du cessez-le-feu par Israël au Liban. Or sur le front libanais, la situation s'est encore durcie ces dernières heures. Des frappes israéliennes près de la ville de Tyr ont fait ce matin au moins 6 morts. Le sud du Liban en particulier est la cible de nombreuses frappes par l'État hébreu, ainsi que la banlieue sud de Beyrouth. Précisions de Serge Berberi, correspondant de France 24 à Beyrouth.

france24fr.title: Le forum économique russe perturbé par des frappes ukrainiennes
france24fr.description: En réponse aux attaques russes d'il y a deux jours, des drones ukrainiens ont frappé Saint-Pétersbourg ce mercredi, dont le terminal pétrolier de la ville. Un signal fort envoyé par Kiev, au moment où se déroule l'équivalent russe du forum économique de Davos, en présence de Vladimir Poutine. Les explications du Général Dominique Trinquand, ex-chef de la mission militaire française auprès des Nations Unies.

france24fr.title: Plus de 1 000 alpinistes au sommet de l'Everest, une saison record sur le toit du monde
france24fr.description: Plus d'un millier d'alpinistes ont réussi ce printemps à atteindre le sommet du toit du monde. Un record absolu de fréquentation pour l'Everest qui ravive les inquiétudes concernant la surfréquentation de la montagne, en particulier dans l'étroite dernière ligne droite qui mène au sommet.

france24fr.title: Flotte fantôme russe : mise en garde à vue du commandant du pétrolier arraisonné par la France
france24fr.description: Le commandant du Tagor, le pétrolier soupçonné de faire partie de la flotte fantôme russe, arraisonné en Atlantique par la Marine française, a été placé en garde à vue mardi, a annoncé le parquet de Brest.

france24fr.title: Algérie : la justice rejette le pourvoi contre Christophe Gleizes, ouvrant la voie à une grâce
france24fr.description: Les avocats du journaliste français Christophe Gleizes, emprisonné depuis un an en Algérie, ont annoncé, mercredi, que le pourvoi en cassation déposé par le procureur général avait été rejeté par le parquet. Cela "clôture" la procédure judiciaire, ouvrant la voie à une possible grâce du président algérien.

france24fr.title: Réduire notre exposition au cadmium ? Un texte discuté à l’Assemblée
france24fr.description: Une proposition de loi écologiste pour limiter les risques d'exposition au cadmium, un métal lourd et toxique, est débattue ce mercredi à l'Assemblée nationale. Les détracteurs du texte dénoncent une initiative dangereuse pour la compétitivité de l'agriculture française. Récit de Marc Paupe.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump "aimerait" rencontrer Khamenei malgré les frappes qui se poursuivent
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump "aimerait" bien rencontrer le guide suprême iranien, qui n’est toujours pas apparu publiquement depuis sa nomination fin février, malgré les frappes qui se poursuivent dans le Golfe. observador.description: Com "prioridade e urgência", a prestação social única (PSU) será discutida no parlamento dia 12. O Governo corre para transpor a diretiva da transparência salarial. E qual foi a adesão à greve?

observador.title: Reabilitação. Projeto quer resolver divergência no IVA a 6%
observador.description: Projeto-lei dos deputados do PSD prevê "interpretação autêntica" do código do IVA para garantir taxa de 6% a obras feitas em áreas de reabilitação urbana sem operações de reabilitação aprovadas.

observador.title: Verão Quente: o povo de chapéu unido jamais será removido?
observador.description: O que levou Pimenta Machado a abrir esta guerra nas praias agora? Os banhos de mar traumatizantes do tio-tetravô de Nuno Markl. E os números da CGTP sobre a greve em que fica difícil acreditar.

observador.title: As crianças passam 38 horas/semana na escola. É demais?
observador.description: Saíram esta semana os dados da Pordata, com base no Eurostat: as crianças portuguesas entre os 6 e 11 anos passam, em média, 38 horas por semana na escola, o valor mais alto de toda a União Europeia.

observador.title: 17h. Portugal eleito para Conselho de Segurança da ONU
observador.description: Portugal foi eleito à primeiro volta. Mandato começa em 2027 e tem duração de dois anos. Ainda neste jornal, Conselho de Ministros esteve reunido para avaliar o impacto da greve geral.

observador.title: ONU. "É necessária uma refundação das Nações Unidas"
observador.description: Jorge Rodrigues defende que a ONU é incapaz de atuar como mediadora de conflitos. O especialista vê as negociações entre o Irão e EUA com ceticismo e acredita que Trump está a perder poder.

observador.title: Portugal eleito membro do Conselho de Segurança
observador.description: O país vai tornar-se um dos cinco membros não permanentes do órgão de manutenção da paz e segurança da ONU, eleito com 134 de 191 votos no plenário realizado em Nova Iorque esta quarta-feira.

observador.title: Gastos com medidas energéticas fora das regras orçamentais
observador.description: A Comissão Europeia estendeu à energia a cláusula de exclusão para as regras orçamentais europeias das despesas já aplicada à defesa até 2028. Apoios no ISP não contam para a exclusão.

observador.title: 16h. ONU. Portugal pode ser eleito para Conselho Segurança
observador.description: Votação decorre na Assembleia Geral da ONU e é acompanhada pelo ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros. Ainda, a ronda pelos protestos em Lisboa e no Porto antes das declaração de Luís Montenegro.

observador.title: Open Innovation Competition foi marcada pela qualidade
observador.description: Depois do sucesso da 1.ª edição, o Prémio Jorge Ruas foi marcado pela enorme concorrência de elevada qualidade e oriunda de vários países. Chegar à final foi uma vitória - e houve um grande vencedor.

observador.title: Há uma barra de ouro de 20 mil euros escondida na Lapónia
observador.description: Este verão, uma estância de ski finlandesa transforma-se numa zona de verdadeira caça ao tesouro. A partir de 18 de junho, turistas podem começar à procura de uma barra de ouro de 20 mil euros.

observador.title: É possível fazer reformas em Portugal ou não saímos disto?
observador.description: No "Realpolitik", Sérgio Sousa Pinto e Miguel Pinheiro falam sobre a dificuldade em fazer reformas, sobre a polémica da Prestação Social Única e sobre a Operação Imergente.

observador.title: Brasil. Mulher cai no esgoto e fica presa
observador.description: Mulher de 33 anos cai na rede de esgoto no Maracanã, no Rio de Janeiro e sofre ferimentos na cabeça. Tampa de sarjeta estaria mal colocada, após tentativa de furto de cabos, diz autarquia.

observador.title: À mesa com o fogo e os micróbios
observador.description: Estamos a cozinhar contra os micróbios ou com eles? Uma conversa sobre evolução, fermentação e saúde com o chef Alexandre Silva e a cientista Isabel Gordo do GIMM.

observador.title: UE criticada por criar "versão" de lei de imigração do ICE
observador.description: Nova lei permitirá a busca em residências para cumprir ordens de deportação. Menores não acompanhados poderão ser detidos, como medida de "último recurso". Prevista criação de "centros de retorno".

observador.title: 15h. Greve geral. Manifestações já estão na rua
observador.description: Lisboa e Porto já com concentrações. Ainda, enquanto Governo diz que a maioria dos portugueses está a trabalhar, a CGTP acusa o Executivo de estar “alheado da realidade”.

spiegel.title: Russlands Versuche, ukrainischen Drohnen abzuwehren: Die Zebra-LKWs brettern durch die Südukraine
spiegel.description: Russland bemalt seine Militärfahrzeuge wegen ukrainischer Drohnenschläge – und bedient sich wieder einmal im Tierreich. Ob das hilft, ist fraglich. Denn Moskaus Truppen stehen unter Druck.

spiegel.title: Japan: Überwachungskamera filmt Bärenangriff auf Fabrikgelände in Fukushima
spiegel.description: Tausende Bären dringen jedes Jahr in Japans Städte ein. Immer wieder kommt es zu Angriffen und sogar Todesfällen. Den jüngsten Vorfall in Fukushima hat eine Überwachungskamera gefilmt.

spiegel.title: 1860 München – 3. Liga: Traditionsclub muss schon wieder in der Regionalliga neu beginnen
spiegel.description: Es ist ein schmerzhaftes Déjà-vu für 1860 München. Investor Ismaik hat eine Finanzierungszusage nicht eingehalten, der Club stürzt schon wieder in die vierte Liga ab. Dies könnte Folgen bis in den Amateurfußball haben.

spiegel.title: Peter Thiel: Warum die Wiener Festwochen den Talk mit dem US-Milliardär absagten
spiegel.description: Der umstrittene US-Milliardär Peter Thiel sollte am Sonntag bei den Wiener Festwochen als Talkgast auftreten. Dann sagte Festivalintendant Milo Rau die Show ab. Hier erklärt er, warum.

spiegel.title: Eli Lilly: US-Pharmakonzern halbiert Milliardeninvestition in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Der US-Pharmariese Eli Lilly fährt die Investition für den geplanten Produktionsstandort auf den Mindestumfang herunter und verweist auf die Sparpläne der Bundesregierung. Auch ein deutscher Konzern stoppt Investitionen.

spiegel.title: Aldi Nord warnt vor Salmonellen im Basilikum
spiegel.description: Wer geriebenes Basilikum der Marke Le Gusto bei Aldi Nord gekauft hat, sollte das Produkt lieber nicht verzehren: In einer Charge wurden Salmonellen nachgewiesen.

spiegel.title: Michelle Obama: Arbeit nervt? Durchhalten, rät die Ex-First Lady der Gen Z
spiegel.description: Michelle Obama findet, junge Menschen sollten auch frustrierende Jobs aushalten – das bereite auf Führungsaufgaben vor. Immerhin war sie einst selbst offenbar eine selbstbewusste und ehrgeizige Jobanfängerin.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Netanyahu sieht Konflikt mit Teheran noch nicht am Ende
spiegel.description: Während US-Präsident Donald Trump über Verhandlungen mit Teheran spricht, sendet Israel ein gegensätzliches Zeichen. Und: Trump bestätigt Bericht über wütendes Telefonat.

spiegel.title: NBA-Finals 2026: Das müssen Sie zu den NBA-Finals wissen
spiegel.description: Die New York Knicks und die San Antonio Spurs spielen ab heute Nacht um die NBA-Meisterschaft. Kann man das in Deutschland schauen? Kommt es zum Showdown zwischen Donald Trump und New Yorks Bürgermeister Mamdani? Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: VfL Wolfsburg: Tobias Strobl vom SC Verl wird neuer Cheftrainer
spiegel.description: Der erste Bundesliga-Abstieg seit knapp 30 Jahren zwingt den VfL Wolfsburg, sich neu aufzustellen. Dafür geht der Club auf der Trainerposition neue Wege.

spiegel.title: Rheinmetall verkauft Autozuliefergeschäft
spiegel.description: Einen Teil seines Geschäfts machte der Düsseldorfer Rüstungskonzern bisher als Kfz-Zulieferer. Bis zum Ende des Jahres will er den Geschäftszweig veräußern – weil sich das Waffengeschäft mehr lohnt.

spiegel.title: Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: So könnte das BSW der AfD zur Macht verhelfen
spiegel.description: Schafft die Wagenknecht-Partei den Sprung in den Magdeburger Landtag, könnte sie zur Königsmacherin in Sachsen-Anhalt werden – und womöglich einen AfD-Mann an die Macht bringen. Wie wahrscheinlich ist das?

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Sitz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat, Angriff auf Sankt Petersburg, Wildschweine
spiegel.description: Wadephul scheitert in New York. Putin blamiert sich in Sankt Petersburg. Und ein Wildschwein wütet in Nürnberg. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Digitale Unabhängigkeit: So will die EU-Kommission die Marktmacht von Big Tech brechen
spiegel.description: Europa soll unabhängiger werden von digitaler Infrastruktur aus den USA. Die EU-Kommission hat jetzt ein Maßnahmenpaket vorgestellt. Das steckt im »Tech Sovereignty Package«.

spiegel.title: Düren – Köln: Mann klammert sich nach Parkplatzstreit an weiterfahrenden Lkw
spiegel.description: Ein 47-Jähriger soll ein bis zwei Autobahnkilometer auf dem Kühlergrill eines Lastwagens mitgefahren sein. Dessen Fahrer wollte sich offenbar wegen eines Streits über einen kaputten Außenspiegel aus dem Staub machen.

spiegel.title: Uno-Sicherheitsrat: Deutschland scheitert mit Bewerbung für nicht-ständigen Sitz
spiegel.description: Portugal und Österreich haben sich durchgesetzt: Deutschland wird beim Uno-Sicherheitsrat als nicht ständiges Mitglied nicht dabei sein. Außenminister Johann Wadephul war bis zuletzt optimistisch gewesen.

spiegel.title: Rätsel des Alltags: Warum sind Schnecken so langsam?
spiegel.description: Gemächlich kriechen sie über Wiesen, durch Gärten und Wälder. Die meisten Schnecken sind lahm unterwegs. Ist das nicht gefährlich für die Tiere? Wieso hat sich die Natur das so ausgedacht? DEIN SPIEGEL erklärt’s.

spiegel.title: Ökologischer Fußabdruck von künstlicher Intelligenz: Wie stark schaden Sie der Umwelt, wenn Sie der KI eine Frage stellen?
spiegel.description: Ein Bericht der Vereinten Nationen beziffert, wie viel Strom und Wasser künstliche Intelligenz angeblich verschlingt. Die Zahlen sind gewaltig, aber auch umstritten.

elpais.title: La UCO constata “al menos” tres reuniones de Leire Díez con la directora de la Guardia Civil, a la que instó a iniciar una “investigación interna” contra la Unidad
elpais.description: El sumario del ‘caso Leire’ recoge que la supuesta ‘fontanera’ del PSOE mantuvo además conversaciones de WhatsApp con Mercedes González, que esta borró

elpais.description: Este agente fue uno de los tres a los que la UCO tomó declaración como testigos el 27 de mayo

elpais.title: La UCO afirma que el puesto de alta dirección en la Diputación de Badajoz estaba “predeterminado” para el hermano de Sánchez
elpais.description: La Guardia Civil señala al exlíder del PSOE extremeño, Miguel Ángel Gallardo, como el instigador de las supuestas irregularidades

elpais.title: “Llegaron los cambios”: más diversidad en la polémica Casita de Bad Bunny
elpais.description: Tras las críticas por la selección de mujeres normativas, en el tercer concierto en Madrid desconocidos de distintas tallas, edades y sexo bailan con famosos como el actor Noah Schnapp

elpais.title: Marc Giró: “No estamos para equidistancias, soy radicalmente de izquierdas y antifascista, ¿existe esta transparencia con otros presentadores?”
elpais.description: El presentador analiza su primer mes en La Sexta con ‘Cara al show’, su nuevo ‘late night’

elpais.title: El león de las cavernas no era un león: el ADN revela una especie con casi dos millones de años de historia propia
elpais.description: Un estudio analiza 12 genomas del ‘Panthera spelaea’ y descubre que su linaje se separó del león africano mucho antes de lo que se pensaba. Los cruces entre ambas especies eran controlados por las glaciaciones

elpais.title: Leo Messi, Premio Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes 2026
elpais.description: El astro argentino, ganador de ocho Balones de Oro y considerado uno de los mejores futbolistas de la historia, recibe el trofeo antes de encarar su último Mundial

elpais.title: El Princesa de Asturias, el premio con el que seguramente no contaba Leo Messi
elpais.description: La celeridad obliga a reparar en la figura del 10 cuando se reconoce su trayectoria, talento, comportamiento y solidaridad con un premio como el recibido este miércoles

elpais.title: Messi: el mejor artesano
elpais.description: Lo ganó todo con el Barça y tiene el récord de balones de oro. Hace cuatro años, en Qatar, se quitó la espina mundialista. En vísperas de su sexta Copa del Mundo, suma a su lista de galardones el Premio Princesa de Asturias de los Deportes 2026

elpais.title: La profe y el poli
elpais.description: La maestra no se habría estampado así contra el asfalto si el brazo armado de la ley no contuviese también el desprecio de una parte no pequeña de la sociedad hacia quienes se manifiestan

elpais.title: Solo un mierda quiere ser profesor
elpais.description: Cómo y por qué el discurso de la extrema derecha contra la educación pública se propaga y condiciona la vida y las elecciones

elpais.title: ¿Qué queréis que haga Bad Bunny ahora?
elpais.description: Cuando uno monta un escaparate no es para enseñar lo mejor que tiene, sino lo que cree más fácil vender

elpais.title: No estás solo, eres invisible
elpais.description: Las sociedades se sostienen sobre vínculos de reciprocidad y confianza y cuando dejamos de vernos y reconocernos el resultado es una comunidad más fragmentada

elpais.title: Pedro Sánchez anuncia que el Gobierno presentará el proyecto de Presupuestos para 2027
elpais.description: El presidente expresa su determinación de culminar la legislatura en la reunión anual del Cercle d’Economia

elpais.title: El juez del ‘caso Plus Ultra’ pide una tasación preliminar de las joyas de Zapatero
elpais.description: El magistrado Calama quiere saber “su naturaleza, autenticidad y valor económico” además del “fabricante”

elpais.title: El PP acepta en Castilla y León la “prioridad nacional” y cede a Vox la política medioambiental y cultural
elpais.description: Los ultras asumen una vicepresidencia y tres consejerías para investir a Mañueco presidente de un gobierno de coalición. El PP se queda la gestión de los incendios

nyt.title: War Games and Warnings on Strait of Hormuz Went Unheeded by Trump
nyt.description: Over the past two decades, Iran repeatedly threatened to close down the waterway. President Trump underestimated Iran’s ability to do so.

nyt.title: Out of Time to Delay, House to Vote on Trump’s Power to Continue War in Iran
nyt.description: A measure to direct the president to halt U.S. engagement in Iran had been on track to pass in late May, but Republican leaders postponed action. They have run out of time to delay the vote.

nyt.title: A Trump Endorsement Falls Flat: 4 Election Takeaways From Iowa and Beyond
nyt.description: The president’s pick for governor of Iowa lost his primary, while Democrats in the state chose their nominee in what they hope will be a competitive Senate race.

nyt.title: 5 Takeaways From the California Primary Election
nyt.description: Without a dominant candidate in the governor’s race, Democratic voters ultimately wanted to ensure that their party wasn’t shut out of the general election.

nyt.title: Why Democrats Are Hopeful About Making Gains in Iowa
nyt.description: After voting twice for Barack Obama, Iowa swung to the right. But the state has been hit hard economically and by Trump policies while growing disenchanted with its leaders.

nyt.title: Trump Aims New Tariffs at 59 Countries and the European Union
nyt.description: Trump administration officials said they planned to impose levies of up to 12.5 percent on countries that failed to crack down on goods made with forced labor.

nyt.title: New Intelligence Role Puts Bill Pulte’s Housing Agenda in Doubt
nyt.description: Mr. Pulte has had difficulty boosting the housing market as head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency. Now he will also serve as acting intelligence director.

nyt.title: Order Shielding Trump Family From I.R.S. Audits Will Remain, Blanche Says
nyt.description: The acting attorney general said the administration was preserving a broad order protecting the president and his family from audits of already filed returns, despite dropping a $1.8 billion payout fund.

nyt.title: For Knicks’ Owner James Dolan, a Title Might Finally Stop Some Boos
nyt.description: James Dolan, the longtime owner of the N.B.A. team, has faced years of jeers. Could a championship change all that?

nyt.title: Want Courtside Seats for the Knicks? Be Rich, Famous and a Die-Hard Fan.
nyt.description: Prime tickets on the floor for the N.B.A. Finals are coveted and very hard to get. The No. 1 requirement: You must love the Knicks.

nyt.title: Bari Weiss Speaks on Scott Pelley’s ’60 Minutes’ Firing: ‘That’s the Path That He Chose’
nyt.description: In her first public comments on the firing, Ms. Weiss, the CBS News editor in chief, said that the longtime correspondent had “broken” the trust in the newsroom.

nyt.title: A New Play, ‘Kenrex,’ Revisits the Story of a Bully’s Unsolved Murder
nyt.description: A man was shot dead surrounded by witnesses in Skidmore, Mo., but no one was ever prosecuted. Now that act of vigilante justice has inspired the play “Kenrex.”

nyt.title: Charleston’s Charm Hides Bloody History of Revolutionary War in South Carolina
nyt.description: Some of the fiercest battles took place in South Carolina, but its part in the fight for independence is often overlooked. Our reporter found history, myths, beauty and contradiction across the Lowcountry landscapes.

nyt.title: Only the Right Tests Can Stop This Ebola Outbreak. Congo Has Hardly Any.
nyt.description: A chronic lack of investment in development of better tests has left clinicians blind and allows deadly viruses to spread unchecked.

nyt.title: At Interlochen, Where Jeffrey Epstein’s Shadow Still Lingers
nyt.description: The arts school and camp is still contending with the fallout from its former ties to Mr. Epstein, an alumnus and donor accused of preying on two girls he met there.

nyt.title: The Big Questions About Jeffrey Epstein: What The Times Has Learned
nyt.description: Here is what we know about the sexual predator whose secrets spurred an international reckoning over money, power and complicity. Check back for updates.

nyt.title: How Taylor Swift Writes a Song, In Her Own Words
nyt.description: The artist shares stories behind some of her biggest hits, her love of a “rant bridge” and how life in the public eye informs the stories she tells in her songs.

nyt.title: This Man Should Not Be in Charge of National Intelligence
nyt.description: Pulte’s one evident qualification is his eagerness to advance the president’s political revenge campaign.

republika.description: L’azienda sanitaria del Friuli Venezia Giulia alla sua richiesta di accedere alla procedura in Italia aveva detto no. Cappato: “Una violenza inflitta dallo Stato"

republika.description: Il procuratore capo D’Alessio: “Non c’è collaborazione, dobbiamo sfaldare il muro di omertà”. Un carabiniere pochi istanti prima aveva redarguito i due ventenni pachistani, poi il rogo e i quattro morti

republika.description: Era in vantaggio per 6-3 4-1, poi è stata sconfitta 3-6 7-5 6-0 dalla russa Diana Shnaider

republika.description: “Falso movimento” girato nel 1974 con Kinski, all'epoca 13enne, non verrà proiettato finché “non verrà trovato un accordo” ha aggiunto il regista che ha chiesto di aprire un dibattito sul cinema "controverso" del Novecento

republika.title: Kostyuk alla russa Andreeva: “Non so come faccia a dormire mentre il suo Paese uccide altre persone”
republika.description: L’ucraina affronterà la russa nella semifinale del Roland Garros

republika.title: Emanuele Pozzolo, il “combinaguai” della destra: dalle beghe di gioventù allo sparo di Capodanno
republika.description: Il deputato, ora approdato al partito di Vannacci, ha avuto un incidente mentre guidava in stato di ebbrezza nel Biellese. Ma è solo l’ultimo episodio imbarazzante che lo vede coinvolto, tra questioni politiche e giudiziarie

republika.title: L’informazione di Repubblica conviene due volte: abbonati e ricevi un buono Amazon
republika.description: Scegli l'abbonamento digitale su misura per te a partire da soli 24€ all'anno: accedi a inchieste, podcast e sfoglio quotidiano e ottieni subito un bonus fino a 20 euro da spendere per i tuoi acquisti online

republika.title: Duecento euro in più al mese per gli under 35, Schlein: “L’Italia diventi un paese per giovani”
republika.description: La segretaria del Pd, insieme al deputato Marco Sarracino, ha presentato una proposta di legge che sancisca il diritto a restare

republika.title: Ue, ok alla clausola di salvaguardia per energia. Giorgetti: “Soddisfatto, accolte nostre proposte”
republika.description: L’Italia resta in procedura deficit eccessivo. Dalla scuola alla sanità, allo sfruttamento del lavoro. Ecco tutte le raccomandazioni nel pacchetto primaverile della Commissione

republika.description: Uno studio sul microbioma dell'Uomo venuto dal ghiaccio ha individuato microrganismi adattati al freddo che potrebbero accompagnare la mummia da millenni. I ricercatori hanno già sperimentato la produzione di lievito madre e guardano a possibili applicazioni nell'industria alimentare

republika.title: Grazia a Nicole Minetti, Procura generale dà parere positivo: “False le notizie su festini e droga”
republika.description: Dopo le verifiche sulla concessione del provvedimento di clemenza, l’atto trasmesso da Milano al ministero della Giustizia: “Adozione del bambino regolare. Ed è in gravi condizioni di salute”. Nordio trasmette gli atti al Quirinale

republika.title: Legnano, i candidati di Fratelli d’Italia fanno il saluto romano. Elly Schlein: “Vergogna assoluta”
republika.description: Gira l’immagine risalente sembra al periodo Covid di Nicola Cavallari e Francesco Terreni, segretario cittadino del partito di Giorgia Meloni

republika.title: L’Ucraina colpisce raffinerie nella regione di San Pietroburgo mentre si apre il Forum economico
republika.description: L’aeroporto Pulkovo costretto a rallentare il traffico. Esplosioni in un terminale portuale. Zelensky conferma gli “attacchi a lungo raggio”

republika.title: Perché la Russia ora alza i toni contro l’Europa: “Il vostro sogno di pace è finito”
republika.description: A Mosca l'Unione Europea viene equiparata alla Germania nazista. Un'escalation contro l'Unione potrebbe offrire al Cremlino il pretesto per una nuova mobilitazione.

npr.title: Greetings from Porto, whose lanes are lined with colorful textiles

new-sci.description: Our understanding of the electromagnetic spectrum goes back to Isaac Newton, but astronomers are still finding new ways to employ it. new-sci.title: How human error became a weapon against large language models
new-sci.description: Alan Turing proposed a test for machine intelligence: could a computer convince a human it was human? We have begun conducting the same test on ourselves, writes Max Moser

new-sci.title: Do turmeric and curcumin have any actual health benefits?
new-sci.description: Turmeric is heralded for its anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties, but columnist Alice Klein finds that the evidence for this is shaky. Taking high doses of its curcumin extract in supplement form can be risky

new-sci.title: Huge study of Alzheimer’s genetics identifies new drug targets
new-sci.description: Almost 50 more genes have been flagged as being linked to Alzheimer’s, along with changes in activity in crucial cells that disappear as dementia progresses

new-sci.title: Capitalism has warped our understanding of ecology and life’s origins

new-sci.title: How a radical new view of life could reveal its origin – and aliens

phys-org.description: Ahead of major soccer tournaments, a research team led by Achim Zeileis of the University of Innsbruck and Andreas Groll of TU Dortmund University calculates the chances of winning for all participating teams. For the 2026 World Cup in Canada, Mexico, and the United States, their model identifies Spain as the slight favorite with 14.5%. phys-org.title: Portable UV spectrometer can detect air pollutants across 2.5 km with high precision
phys-org.description: Birgitta Schultze-Bernhardt and her team at the Institute of Experimental Physics at Graz University of Technology (TU Graz) have developed a new type of UV dual-comb spectrometer that detects gaseous air pollutants with unrivaled accuracy and sensitivity. Using ultraviolet double laser light, the device measures the concentration of harmful gases such as formaldehyde within half a second.

phys-org.title: Self-regulation can curb students' overconfidence in AI
phys-org.description: The rapid emergence of generative AI in higher education has raised concerns about students' reliance on the use of these tools for academic and personal tasks. Although generative AI can boost productivity and creativity, key learning skills may be undermined by overreliance on it.

phys-org.title: Chip-scale 'acoustic atom' controls sound waves to imitate atomic energy levels and advance computing
phys-org.description: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. What goes up must come down. Physical laws like these govern all of the natural world—except for the tiny internal components of today's microprocessors, which operate according to the unique and complicated rules of quantum physics.

phys-org.title: Why 'charming' matters: Study reveals the power of puffery on consumer behavior
phys-org.description: Big brands have built empires on slogans, declaring themselves the best among their competitors. These claims—glowing, subjective and impossible to verify—fall under what marketers call puffery. For decades, they've been treated as harmless fluff, waved through the court system on the assumption that consumers tune them out.

phys-org.title: Spider webs capture hidden fungal diversity in Thai rice fields
phys-org.description: A new study published in the open-access Biodiversity Data Journal suggests that spider webs—particularly those incorporating environmental debris—can serve as natural, non-destructive collectors of fungal material in agricultural ecosystems. The findings show that viable fungi can be recovered from these structures, including lineages that may represent previously undocumented diversity.

phys-org.title: Studying impact flashes to detect missile and meteorite composition
phys-org.description: Southwest Research Institute, or SwRI, is studying impact flashes generated by high-speed collisions. One application of understanding impact flashes is to remotely identify what materials are involved in the collisions. Advances in understanding optical impact flashes can be highly beneficial for missile defense, making it possible to determine the composition of an intercepted missile and its payload.

phys-org.title: HETDEX opens massive Cosmic Noon dataset to scientists, novices and AI
phys-org.description: The Hobby-Eberly Telescope Dark Energy Experiment (HETDEX)—which recently completed the largest survey ever taken of the early universe—has released all of its immense, information-rich database to the public. phys-org.title: UN calculates nation-sized environmental footprints for AI and data centers
phys-org.description: The environmental footprint of data centers already rivals some of the world's largest countries, according to a United Nations University report, which also predicts their water and energy use and pollution will double in just four years as use of artificial intelligence grows.

phys-org.title: 'BBQ sauce' phase may link little red dots to quasars
phys-org.description: Everyone knows that finding the right sauce recipe can make or break a barbecue, but now astronomers are using BBQSORS (pronounced "barbecue sauce") as part of the recipe to explain quasars, some of the brightest objects in the universe. These results were made possible by data from a new instrument on the Subaru Telescope.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Experts discuss rise of profanity from politicians
phys-org.description: In American politics, cursing and "four-letter words" are no longer confined to hot mics or hidden behind closed doors. Politicians and pundits are increasingly using so-called "bad words" in speeches, social media posts and campaign ads. phys-org.title: Mars mission ends: NASA declares Maven dead after six months of silence
phys-org.description: After six months of radio silence, NASA's Maven spacecraft at Mars has been declared dead.

phys-org.title: Deep-Earth seismic anomalies may be explained by newly discovered manganese compound
phys-org.description: Scientists know that manganese, in its various oxide forms, plays a significant role in Earth's geochemical cycles. However, the exact forms of manganese, their abundance and the mechanisms behind these cycles that occur in Earth's deep, high-pressure interior are not well understood. phys-org.title: Why do male chimpanzees throw rocks at the same trees for more than a decade?
phys-org.description: Walking through the savanna-woodland landscape of Boé National Park, Guinea-Bissau, you might encounter a tree covered in gnarled scars, with an accumulation of rocks surrounding its base.

phys-org.title: Climate change may shift hailstorms toward Earth's poles—new study
phys-org.description: Everyone has a storm story—whether it's that time you just escaped a downpour, or the hailstorm that wrote off your car. Even though hailstorms are relatively rare, they cause significant damage. Two new studies shed light on how hail might change as the world warms.

phys-org.title: The push to standardize ESG scores could make corporate greenwashing easier, not harder
phys-org.description: Three-quarters of S&P 500 companies now tie a portion of their CEO's pay to environmental, social and governance (ESG) metrics. They typically include carbon emissions, workforce diversity and worker safety, among others.

phys-org.title: Hail conditions on the move as winter crops face rising risk
phys-org.description: A hailstorm can undo a season's work in minutes. It can strike quickly and unevenly, shredding wheat, bruising fruit, flattening crops—while also leaving neighboring paddocks untouched. In a new Nature Climate Change study, scientists from UNSW Sydney say the geography and seasonality of that risk is changing.

phys-org.title: A lot of 'recycled' plastic is being burned overseas—and causing widespread pollution linked to health problems
phys-org.description: Picture a pile of trash the size of Manhattan and taller than one and a half Empire State Buildings. That's how much plastic waste the world is predicted to be generating every year by 2050 if nothing is done to change course.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.
